target_frame.title: Intermittent cold-room delivery gaps
target_frame.problem: A regional food distributor finds that some refrigerated deliveries arrive above its internal receiving temperature range, although the loading records show acceptable temperatures. The operations manager must decide what to investigate next and which temporary handling changes are justified before the next fortnight of deliveries.
known_context: There are three loading bays, two contracted carriers and routes lasting between forty minutes and four hours.
Drivers record departure and arrival times; receiving staff take a single temperature reading from one package per delivery.
Loading-bay logs record room temperature every fifteen minutes, but packages are not individually tracked between staging and loading.
The recent exceptions occur on both short and long routes. Receiving methods differ between customer sites.
A small pool of reusable temperature loggers is available, but the team cannot instrument every package or cancel routine deliveries.
target_frame.uncertainty: The manager does not know whether the exceptions mainly arise before loading, in transit, during receiving, or from differences in measurement. Multiple contributors may be present.
target_frame.decision_need: Identify a feasible investigation and defensible interim action without claiming that the existing endpoint records locate the cause.
constraints: Normal food-handling requirements remain in force.
Staff can add limited observations for two weeks; there is no budget for fleet replacement.

source_instrument.state: Several plausible explanations can account for an uncertain situation, and available evidence may fit more than one of them.
source_instrument.operation: State the competing explanations explicitly, evaluate each item of evidence against all of them, emphasize evidence that is inconsistent with particular explanations, and test the sensitivity of the resulting comparison to uncertain evidence or assumptions.
source_instrument.signal: The evidence forms a comparative pattern of consistency and inconsistency across the competing explanations, with some items discriminating among them more strongly than others.
source_instrument.inference: Explanations with greater important inconsistency can be weakened or eliminated, leaving a smaller set of alternatives that better survives the observed evidence.
source_instrument.limit: Missing hypotheses, dependent or unreliable evidence, subjective consistency judgments, poor assessment of diagnosticity, and shared assumptions can make the comparison misleading. Surviving contradiction is not proof that the remaining explanation is true.

mapping.state: Investigate four competing explanations: warming during staging/loading, warming in transit, warming during receiving, and differences or errors in measurement. Include combinations; these mechanisms need not be mutually exclusive. Existing bay temperatures and single-package arrival readings do not establish package temperatures throughout the journey or locate a cause. Assume provisionally that loggers can be deployed safely and linked to selected packages; verify this before starting.
mapping.operation: For two weeks, rotate the available loggers across selected deliveries covering all three bays, both carriers, short and long routes, and different receiving sites where feasible. Include deliveries with and without prior exceptions; record coverage gaps. Identify monitored packages from staging through receipt, synchronize clocks, and record staging, loading, departure, arrival, unloading and receiving-measurement times. Record logger placement and whether it measures package temperature or surrounding air; do not equate these. Check logger and receiving-device performance using approved procedures. At receipt, pair the site's usual reading with a consistent, approved measurement on the tracked package where feasible, documenting method, location and delay without compromising handling. Before reviewing results, write predictions for each explanation. Build an evidence-by-explanation table marking consistency, inconsistency or indeterminate, with reasons and confidence. Evaluate every observation against every explanation, including combined explanations; prioritize reliable contradictions over counts of supporting observations. Repeat the comparison after excluding unreliable readings, treating observations from one delivery as dependent, varying uncertain handoff times and sensor-response assumptions, and separating air from package measurements. Review exceptions promptly and the full comparison at fortnight's end. Stop using a device or procedure if it compromises food handling; flag failed or missing traces as inconclusive and redeploy safely.
mapping.signal: Look for time-localized changes and paired-measurement agreement. A reliable package-relevant rise before loading, followed by stable transit readings, would contradict transit as the sole origin for that monitored package. Acceptable conditions through departure followed by a transit rise would weaken a solely preloading explanation. Acceptable conditions through arrival followed by warming during documented receiving delay would weaken explanations confined to earlier stages. Disagreement between usual and standardized readings would support investigating measurement differences, while agreement on elevated package temperature would weaken measurement differences as the sole explanation. These comparisons require adequate temporal resolution, suitable sensor placement and comparable measurements; otherwise mark the evidence indeterminate. Multiple rises could support combined contributors. No such observations are yet established.
mapping.inference: Weaken explanations in proportion to the importance and reliability of their contradictions, eliminating one only within the scope actually tested. Direct the next investigation toward alternatives that survive and observations that would distinguish them. During the fortnight, reinforce existing cold-staging practices, reduce avoidable unprotected handoff delays, and standardize approved receiving measurements where feasible. Use credible stage-specific evidence to target additional temporary supervision or handling changes at that stage. Apply existing food-handling and disposition requirements whenever a reading triggers them; do not await causal certainty or relax requirements. At fortnight's end, retain justified temporary controls and, if the ranking remains unstable or coverage inadequate, specify a focused next sampling round rather than declare a cause.
mapping.limit: Sparse, selectively monitored packages cannot establish prevalence or clear an entire delivery, carrier, bay or route. Air traces, sensor lag, clock errors, device error, package variability and different measurement locations can create misleading apparent contradictions. Repeated readings and records from one delivery are not independent confirmations. Missing mechanisms, subjective consistency judgments, mistaken diagnosticity and shared assumptions may distort every comparison; sensitivity to these requires an explicitly uncertain conclusion and revised hypotheses or measurements. An internal-range exception alone does not establish food-safety status. Surviving contradiction does not prove an explanation true, and improvement after a temporary change does not by itself establish causation.
